subject: Renewal proposal: ops matrix, GPU add-on and logical fencing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@acme-insights.com>, Acme Insights Procurement <procurement@acme-insights.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: ops matrix, GPU add-on and logical fencing

Ethan / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is the renewal amendment and a first-pass SLA that reflects the capacity expansion we discussed. High-level proposal:

- Reserved capacity: add a dedicated reserved pool of 20 GPUs (A100 equivalent) scoped to Acme Insights' production workloads.
- Logical fencing: configurable tenant separation via reserved pools + strict scheduler rules (details in the attachment).
- Optional node-fencing: for regulated workflows we can reserve a small physically fenced pool (4 GPUs) at an additional premium.
- Term and pricing: 18-month renewal term tying the additional reserved capacity to a committed discount (15% on the incremental reservation).
- Throughput target: aggregate throughput SLO for the reserved pool; see SLA_Detail_v1.pdf.

Next steps: please confirm you want the node-fenced option and we will: 1) lock pricing in the amendment (attached), 2) add the network diagram/stateful routing notes, and 3) schedule an ops kickoff.

Attachments: Redwood_Amendment_Draft.pdf, SLA_Detail_v1.pdf

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@acme-insights.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Insights Procurement <procurement@acme-insights.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: ops matrix, GPU add-on and logical fencing

Vivek,

Thanks — this looks promising. A couple items procurement and our security team asked us to clarify before we sign: 

1) "Tenant separation": we need to know whether logical fencing means a single tenant-wide reserved pool or whether we can provision per-customer isolation inside our account. For our regulated customers we may need strict separation.

2) Do you provide a formal commitment for noisy-neighbor mitigation and a throughput SLO per tenant (e.g., 95th percentile latency / requests-per-second guarantees)? We run variable peak loads and want predictable tail latency.

3) Procurement asked for a network diagram and a SOC 2 attestation reference (or link) to include in the purchase file.

If you can answer 1–2 in writing and drop the network diagram, procurement can review the amendment this week. Also please outline the incremental monthly cost for the optional 4-GPU node-fenced pool.

Thanks,
Ethan Brooks
Head of Platform, Acme Insights
ethan.brooks@acme-insights.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal: ops matrix, GPU add-on and logical fencing

Vivek / Lauren — answering the technical points Ethan raised so we have a single explanation to send to the customer: 

1) Tenant separation options: 
   - Logical fencing (default): a named reserved pool scoped to Acme Insights with per-workload queueing and strict GPU allocation rules. This provides soft isolation — workloads cannot preempt each other and scheduling ensures reserved capacity for prioritized queues. This is our typical approach for multi-tenant accounts.
   - Per-customer isolation (optional): we can create sub-pools per Acme customer that are logically isolated inside your account. This adds orchestration overhead but gives stronger isolation at the scheduling layer.
   - Node-fencing (optional, regulatory): physically pinning containers/VMs to a set of dedicated nodes (the 4-GPU pool) so workloads run on exclusive hardware.

2) Throughput / SLOs:
   - For the 20-GPU reserved pool we can commit to an aggregate throughput target (example: sustained X requests/min with 95th pct latency under 200ms for payloads under 1k tokens). We will not publish per-GPU microbenchmarks in the contract, but we will add a pass/fail measurement and a monthly credit if the pool fails the SLA (we typically use a credit equal to a small percentage of monthly fees). Exact metrics to be captured in the SLA document.

3) Artifacts: network_diagram_v2.png is ready and I included pointers to our SOC 2 report URL in the drive link.

Operational notes: provisioning the 20-GPU pool takes ~5 business days after amendment signature; node-fenced pools require additional lead time (7–10 business days) because of capacity scheduling.

Let me know if you want me to include example benchmark runs for typical Acme workloads — we can run a short targeted test against a staging pool.

—Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal: ops matrix, GPU add-on and logical fencing

Team — drafting negotiation guidance for the amendment: 

- Term: propose 18 months (compromise between Acme's preference for 12 and our 24).
- Price: 15% discount on the incremental reserved capacity; include an optional add-on for the 4-GPU node-fenced pool at a fixed monthly fee (we suggest $14,400/mo as a starting point).
- SLA credit: include a simple remediation clause — if monthly measured throughput for the reserved pool is below the agreed threshold two months in a row, Acme receives a 5% credit of that month's reserved fees and we commit to an ops remediation plan.
- Signature flow: procurement needs the network diagram + SOC 2 link (we have both linked in our HubSpot deal).

If Marcus is comfortable with the technical wording above, I'll finalize the amendment PDF and send to Ethan with the network diagram attached.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@acme-insights.com>, Acme Insights Procurement <procurement@acme-insights.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal amendment & capacity confirmation — Acme Insights

Ethan / Procurement,

Thanks for the quick follow-up. Per our internal review and Marcus' notes, here is a concise summary of what we're prepared to include in the signed amendment: 

- Reserved pools: one primary reserved pool of 20 GPUs (A100-class) dedicated to Acme Insights' production workloads.
- Tenant separation: logical fencing will be applied by default (named reserved pool + strict scheduler queues). If you require per-customer sub-pools we will provision those as separate logical sub-pools (recommended for high regulatory customers).
- Node-fenced option: we will provision an optional physically fenced pool (4 GPUs) for PII/regulatory workloads at the quoted add-on price; lead time 7–10 business days.
- Term & pricing: 18-month renewal term with 15% discount on the incremental reserved capacity. Add-on fees for the node-fenced pool will be listed in the amendment.
- SLA & credits: SLA_Detail_v1.pdf captures measurement and credit approach — we propose a 5% monthly credit if the reserved pool fails the throughput/latency measurement per the SLA for two consecutive months.
- Timeline: provisioning for the 20-GPU pool begins within 5 business days of signature; ops kickoff scheduled in week 1 of provisioning.

Attachments included: Redwood_Amendment_Draft.pdf, SLA_Detail_v1.pdf, network_diagram_v2.png

If this summary matches Acme's expectations, please let me know and I'll route the amendment for signature and lock the capacity. If procurement needs any additional artifacts for the PO package, tell us what else is required and we'll push it over.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123
redwood.com
